# Lunch Sorted

> A school-lunch planner for parents. Answer three questions and it plans a week of packed school lunches from foods your kid will eat, matches them so each box goes together, keeps your school's rules, and writes the shopping list.

Lunch Sorted is made by a parent in Maryland (Lila Bloom Enterprises). It is a web app at https://lunchsorted.app/app/ that installs to a phone's home screen and works offline. An iPhone app is in review.

## Who it is for

The parent who packs a school lunch, usually for a child in kindergarten through fifth grade. A child only ever sees one screen, the kid's pick, when a parent hands over the phone, and is never asked for anything.

## What it does

- Plans a main, a side, a fruit and a sweet for every school day, from the family's own food list, paired so a box makes sense (crunchy against soft, protein when the main is light).
- Keeps school rules: nuts, seeds and sesame, dairy, gluten, egg, soy or fish kept out; cold lunches only; no ice pack; a short eating time; no chocolate or candy. A food that breaks a rule is flagged, never deleted.
- Builds one shopping list for the week, grouped by aisle.
- Asks after school what came home; a food that comes home twice in a row rests for three weeks.
- Plans more than one lunchbox, matched, with each box keeping its own rules.

## What it costs

Free for one lunchbox, for good. The Household plan adds every lunchbox, a second parent's phone, a caretaker's pack list, your own foods and recipes, the kid's pick, the after-school review and a pantry that remembers. Every new household gets the whole plan for three weeks, no card. Prices: https://lunchsorted.app/

## What it does not do

It does not count calories or give nutrition, medical or allergy advice. It does not order groceries.

## Privacy

Signed out, lunches stay on the phone. The planner loads no analytics and no advertising. Details: https://lunchsorted.app/privacy.html

## Answers

- [Help](https://lunchsorted.app/help.html): what it is, how the week is picked, school rules, what is free, sign-in, offline.
